input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having some trouble with my mobile data. It either stops working or is very slow, and I really need it to be excellent. I’m not very good with technology, so I’d appreciate some help getting it fixed. I don’t have Wi-Fi, so I rely on my mobile internet. Can you help me get excellent internet speed on my phone?
My name is John Smith, and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started. What do I need to do next?

Oh, I definitely don’t want to change my plan—I just want to add more data for now. Let’s add 2GB, please. I really need the internet to be excellent, not just a little better. What do I need to do next?
I’m a bit nervous about restarting my phone—will I lose any of my photos or anything important if I do that? I really don’t want to mess anything up. Can you reassure me before I try it?
Okay, I restarted my phone like you said. Now I see a little airplane symbol at the top of my screen. Is that supposed to be there? My internet still isn’t working. What should I do next?

Alright, I turned off Airplane Mode and the airplane symbol is gone now. I see some bars and something that says 5G at the top, but I also see a little symbol that looks like data is disabled. My internet still isn’t working. What should I do next?

Okay, I turned on Mobile Data and now I see a little phone symbol at the top. But there’s also something that says “Data Saver.” My internet still doesn’t seem very fast. Is there something else I should do?

Alright, I turned off Data Saver mode. Now I just see the bars, 5G, and the little phone symbol at the top. Should I try using the internet now, or is there something else I need to do to make sure it’s excellent?
I tried to use the internet, but it still isn’t working. I even tried to check the speed, but it says there’s no connection. What should I do now? I really need excellent internet speed.
I checked, and my SIM card seems to be active and working—there aren’t any error messages about it. What should I do next?

I checked my APN settings, and it says the APN name is “internet” and there’s something about an MMSC URL. I’m not sure if that’s right or not. Should I still reset the APN settings, or is there something else I should do? I really just want my internet to be excellent.

I reset the APN settings and restarted my phone, but I still can’t get any internet connection. The speed test still says there’s no connection. I’m starting to get a bit frustrated—why isn’t this working? I really need excellent internet speed. What else can I try?

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hello, I’m having some trouble with my mobile data. It either stops working or is very slow, and I really need it to be excellent. I’m not very good with technology, so I’d appreciate some help getting it fixed. I don’t have Wi-Fi, so I rely on my mobile internet. Can you help me get excellent internet speed on my phone?

Thank you for reaching out about your mobile data issue. I can help you troubleshoot and improve your mobile internet speed.

To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide one of the following:
- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth (in YYYY-MM-DD format), or
- Your customer ID (if you have it)?

Once I have this information, I can check your account and guide you through the steps to improve your mobile data speed.

You have already used 15.1GB this month, which means you have exceeded your plan’s data limit. This is likely why your mobile data is slow or not working.

You have two options to restore excellent internet speed:
1. Add more data to your line (up to 2GB at $2.00 per GB).
2. Change to a plan with a higher data limit.

To ensure the new data is applied, please restart your phone. After rebooting, your mobile data should work at full speed again.

If you have any other issues or need more help, just let me know!
I’m a bit nervous about restarting my phone—will I lose any of my photos or anything important if I do that? I really don’t want to mess anything up. Can you reassure me before I try it?

Rest assured, restarting your phone is a safe process and will not delete any of your photos, messages, apps, or other important information. Restarting simply turns your phone off and then back on, which helps it refresh its connection and apply changes like the new data you just added.

You won’t lose any personal data or settings by restarting. It’s a common and safe step to help fix many phone issues.

If you’re ready, you can go ahead and restart your phone now. If you have any concerns or need step-by-step instructions, just let me know!

Restarting network services...
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
Okay, I restarted my phone like you said. Now I see a little airplane symbol at the top of my screen. Is that supposed to be there? My internet still isn’t working. What should I do next?

The airplane symbol means that Airplane Mode is turned on, which disables all wireless connections—including your mobile data. That’s why your internet isn’t working right now.

To fix this, you need to turn off Airplane Mode. Please look for an option called “Airplane Mode” in your phone’s quick settings (usually by swiping down from the top of your screen) and tap it to turn it off. The airplane symbol should disappear, and your phone should reconnect to the mobile network.

Once you’ve turned off Airplane Mode, check if your internet is working. Let me know if you need step-by-step instructions or if you still have issues after turning it off.

Airplane Mode is now OFF.

Alright, I turned off Airplane Mode and the airplane symbol is gone now. I see some bars and something that says 5G at the top, but I also see a little symbol that looks like data is disabled. My internet still isn’t working. What should I do next?

Thank you for the update. Since you see the 5G symbol and signal bars, your phone is connected to the network, but it looks like mobile data might be turned off.

Please check your phone’s settings and make sure that “Mobile Data” is turned ON. Usually, you can find this option in your quick settings (by swiping down from the top of your screen) or in your phone’s main settings under “Network” or “Connections.”

Once you turn on Mobile Data, your internet should start working. If you need step-by-step instructions or if it’s already on and you’re still having issues, please let me know!

Mobile Data is now ON.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔽 Data Saver | 🔋 80%

Okay, I turned on Mobile Data and now I see a little phone symbol at the top. But there’s also something that says “Data Saver.” My internet still doesn’t seem very fast. Is there something else I should do?

The “Data Saver” feature can slow down your internet by restricting background data usage to help save data. To get the best speed, you should turn off Data Saver mode.

Please go to your phone’s settings, look for “Data Saver” (it might be under “Network & Internet” or “Connections”), and turn it OFF. Once Data Saver is off, your internet speed should improve.

Let me know once you’ve done this, or if you need help finding the setting!

Data Saver Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Alright, I turned off Data Saver mode. Now I just see the bars, 5G, and the little phone symbol at the top. Should I try using the internet now, or is there something else I need to do to make sure it’s excellent?
Speed test failed: No Connection.
I tried to use the internet, but it still isn’t working. I even tried to check the speed, but it says there’s no connection. What should I do now? I really need excellent internet speed.

Thank you for letting me know. Since you’ve already turned off Airplane Mode, enabled Mobile Data, and disabled Data Saver, but still have no internet connection, let’s try a few more steps:

1. Check if your SIM card is working correctly. Please look for any messages about your SIM card on your phone, or let me know if you see anything unusual (like “No SIM” or “SIM error”).
2. If possible, try removing your SIM card and reinserting it to make sure it’s seated properly.
3. If you don’t see any SIM errors, the next step is to check your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings, which control how your phone connects to the internet.

Could you let me know if you see any SIM card errors or messages? If not, I’ll guide you through checking and resetting your APN settings next.
Your SIM card is active and working.
I checked, and my SIM card seems to be active and working—there aren’t any error messages about it. What should I do next?

Great, since your SIM card is active and working, the next step is to check your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings. Sometimes, incorrect APN settings can prevent your phone from connecting to mobile data.

Please check your APN settings on your phone. If you see anything unusual or if you’re not sure what to look for, you can reset your APN settings to default. After resetting, you’ll need to restart your phone for the changes to take effect.

Would you like step-by-step instructions on how to check or reset your APN settings?

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

Thank you for checking your APN settings. Since you’re still having trouble with your internet connection and you’re unsure about the APN details, it’s a good idea to reset your APN settings to the default values. This often resolves issues with mobile data connectivity.

After you reset your APN settings, you’ll need to restart your phone for the changes to take effect.

Would you like step-by-step instructions on how to reset your APN settings and restart your phone, or do you feel comfortable doing this on your own? Let me know how you’d like to proceed!

APN settings will reset at reboot.
